preamble: The voiced aspirated velar stop [ɡʱ] loses its oral closure and only its breathy component survives, as the voiced glottal fricative [ɦ]. In Middle Indo-Aryan, single intervocalic Sanskrit gh was reduced to h, pronounced [ɦ] as in Sanskrit and Hindi (megha > Prakrit meha, laghu > lahu), and the change is continued in the modern languages.

examples.note: Middle Indo-Aryan reduction of intervocalic aspirates to h; also Assamese meh, Gujarati meh, Punjabi mī̃h (Turner CDIAL 10302)
gh > h intervocalically; the Hindi form shows later metathesis lahu- > halu-

sources: Turner, R. L. (1966). A Comparative Dictionary of the Indo-Aryan Languages, entry 10302 mēghá. https://dsal.uchicago.edu/dictionaries/soas/
